title: The Mice and the Weasels
text:
The mice and the weasels were at war, and the weasels kept winning. After one defeat too many, the mice held a council and decided that the problem was organization. They had no proper commanders, so they fought as a disorderly crowd.

They chose generals from the most distinguished families and the bravest fighters, and divided the army into troops and regiments. To make sure everyone could tell them apart, the new generals fastened tall decorations to their heads, straws or horns that stood up proudly above the ranks. A herald declared war, and the mice marched out in good order.

The battle went badly almost at once. The ordinary mice turned and ran, and each one darted safely into its hole. The generals ran too, but their splendid headgear would not fit through the narrow openings. They were stuck outside, and the weasels caught and ate every one of them.
lesson: Titles and symbols of rank do not make anyone a leader, and they can become a burden when things go wrong. Invest in what helps the people you lead, not in what makes you stand out.
